phrase: Thank you all for joining today's meeting.
useCase: Opening a regular team meeting with a polite welcome
example: Good morning, everyone. Thank you all for joining today's meeting. Let's get started.
practicePrompt: Imagine you are opening a weekly team meeting. Use this phrase to welcome your colleagues.

phrase: I'd like to call this meeting to order.
useCase: Formally opening a board or committee meeting
example: Thank you for being here on time. I'd like to call this meeting to order.
practicePrompt: You are chairing a formal committee meeting. Open the meeting using this phrase.

phrase: Let me start by outlining today's agenda.
useCase: Introducing the meeting agenda at the beginning of a meeting
example: Welcome, everyone. Let me start by outlining today's agenda. We have three main items to cover.
practicePrompt: You are leading a project status meeting. Introduce the agenda using this phrase.

phrase: The purpose of today's meeting is to discuss...
useCase: Stating the objective of the meeting clearly at the start
example: The purpose of today's meeting is to discuss the upcoming product launch timeline and resource allocation.
practicePrompt: You are opening a client review meeting. State the meeting's purpose using this phrase.

phrase: I've invited everyone here today to address...
useCase: Explaining why participants were gathered for the meeting
example: I've invited everyone here today to address the recent changes in our compliance requirements.
practicePrompt: You called a cross-departmental meeting. Explain the reason using this phrase.

phrase: Before we begin, I'd like to quickly go over the ground rules.
useCase: Setting expectations and rules at the start of a collaborative session
example: Before we begin, I'd like to quickly go over the ground rules. Please mute your phones and hold questions until each section is done.
practicePrompt: You are facilitating a brainstorming workshop. Set the ground rules using this phrase.

phrase: We have a lot to cover today, so let's dive right in.
useCase: Transitioning quickly into the meeting content when time is limited
example: Thanks for being here. We have a lot to cover today, so let's dive right in. First item on the agenda is the Q3 budget review.
practicePrompt: You are leading a packed status update meeting. Open with urgency using this phrase.

phrase: I'd like to kick things off by reviewing our action items from last time.
useCase: Opening a recurring meeting by referencing previous follow-ups
example: Good afternoon, everyone. I'd like to kick things off by reviewing our action items from last time before we move to new topics.
practicePrompt: You are chairing a biweekly team sync. Open by referencing past action items using this phrase.

phrase: For those who may not know me, my name is... and I'll be facilitating today's session.
useCase: Introducing yourself as the meeting facilitator when participants may be unfamiliar
example: For those who may not know me, my name is Sarah, and I'll be facilitating today's session on onboarding improvements.
practicePrompt: You are leading a meeting with new stakeholders. Introduce yourself using this phrase.

phrase: I appreciate everyone making time for this discussion.
useCase: Expressing gratitude to participants for attending a specially called meeting
example: I appreciate everyone making time for this discussion. I know schedules are tight, so I'll keep this focused and concise.
practicePrompt: You called an ad-hoc meeting on short notice. Express appreciation using this phrase.
